summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a complex medical history including CAD s/p CABG, atrial fibrillation, COPD, prior strokes, and cerebellar degeneration was admitted for acute left-sided chest and LUQ pain. Initial concern for ACS was ruled out with normal troponins and echocardiogram. Pain was reproducible on exam and worsened with movement, consistent with musculoskeletal etiology, likely costochondritis. Imaging revealed a new moderate left pleural effusion with partial collapse of the left lower lobe, but no signs of infection or pulmonary embolism. A CTA abdomen showed 75% stenosis of the SMA without symptoms of ischemia; vascular surgery recommended outpatient follow-up. The patient remained afebrile with stable vitals, improving WBC, and no respiratory deterioration. He was discharged home with services on a lidocaine patch for pain, with follow-up for repeat chest imaging and vascular surgery evaluation.
